court: Supreme Court, Appellate Division, First Department
holding_summary: Marriage-annulment jurisdiction case holding that substituted service by publication did not confer jurisdiction over a non-resident defendant.
notes: Domicile facts note the couple 'occupying furnished rooms at several different addresses'; purely incidental to jurisdiction/domicile analysis, not a letting or boarding dispute.

cite: Couch v. Farmers' Fire Insurance of York, 64 A.D. 367
holding_summary: Fire insurance policy voided under a 'vacant or unoccupied' clause where the insured left her dwelling unattended for nearly five months.
notes: Retrieved passage discusses an owner's residual 'interest in protection and preservation' of a vacant house for insurance-occupancy purposes; unrelated to compensated letting or lodging.

cite: Safee v. City of Buffalo, 204 A.D. 561
court: Supreme Court, Appellate Division, Fourth Department
holding_summary: Sustained under the police power a Buffalo ordinance licensing and regulating the sale of soft drinks in the wake of Prohibition-era enforcement problems.
notes: Police-power licensing case about soda/soft-drink retailers, not lodging or boarding houses; selector matched on generic 'regulation'/police-power language.

cite: McLean v. F. W. Woolworth Co., 204 A.D. 118
court: Supreme Court, Appellate Division, Third Department
holding_summary: Held that a one-story-height restriction in an 1881 deed was a personal covenant benefiting only the grantor, not a covenant running with the land binding a later-erected building.
notes: Quoted 'nuisance'/occupancy language is from a different case (Clark v. Devoe) cited for covenant-construction principles; the dispute itself concerns building-height restrictions, not lodging or paying occupants.

cite: People ex rel. Van Norder v. Sewer, Water & Street Commission, 90 A.D. 555
holding_summary: Upheld revocation of a hackman's license for soliciting patronage on public streets in violation of statute and license conditions.
notes: Police-power licensing case about cab/hackman regulation on public streets; no connection to lodging or boarding houses despite selector match on 'regulation' language.

holding_summary: Murder conviction reversed for exclusion of physical evidence and erroneous jury instructions on flight and good-character evidence.
notes: Defendant and decedent were rival 'runners' soliciting boarders/lodgers for a seamen's home vs. sailors' boarding houses; boarding-house business mentioned only as employment background to a homicide, not adjudicated.

cite: In re the Transfer Tax on Estate Conveyed in Trust for His Own Benefit of Craig, 97 A.D. 289
holding_summary: Held that remainder interests vested by an 1875 trust deed accrued before enactment of the transfer tax statutes and could not retroactively be taxed.
notes: Transfer-tax/vested-remainder case; 'incident of ownership' language concerns property-right vesting, not letting of dwellings. No lodging or boarding content.

holding_summary: The court held that a boarding-house keeper could not hold a married woman personally liable for her family's board bill absent an express agreement to pay, because the common-law duty to support the family -- and hence liability for necessaries such as board and lodging -- rests presumptively on the husband; the wife's trunks retained under the keeper's claimed lien were ordered released.

quotes.text: furnished to the plaintiff and to Jacob Buhl, her husband, at the request of the plaintiff and her said husband, accommodation, board and lodging

The plaintiff brings this action to recover certain trunks containing her personal wardrobe, or- their value, such trunks being retained by the defendant, a boarding-house keeper, who claims a lien upon the same for the amount of a board bill aggregating something over $150.
liability for necessaries, furnished to the family of a married man is presumptively and primarily upon the husband, unless the wife by express agreement charges herself personally with the same

notes: Occupancy ran roughly May-July 1903 (about two months) before the family departed; treated as ordinary/months rather than unclear given the stated dates.

court: Supreme Court, Appellate Division, First Department
holding_summary: Burglary conviction reversed as against the weight of the evidence where guilt rested only on an alleged admission and property found in the defendant's room.
notes: Defendant's room in a 'furnished rooms house' is mentioned only as the location searched by police after his arrest; the letting arrangement itself is not at issue.

court: Supreme Court, Appellate Division, Second Department
holding_summary: Denied injunctive relief against a building-line covenant violation because the plaintiff herself was violating an identical covenant on her own lot.
notes: Real-property setback/restrictive-covenant dispute between neighboring landowners; no compensated occupancy or lodging issue.

court: Supreme Court, Appellate Division, Third Department
holding_summary: A conditional vendor of a piano who failed to file or deliver a duplicate of his conditional sale contract as required by the 1897 Lien Law could not defeat the claim of a boarding-house keeper who, as a good-faith pledgee, had acquired a statutory lien on the piano left with her by a boarder for an unpaid board bill.

quotes.text: Arthur J. Mann, Mrs. Mann, his wife, and their son became boarders at the boarding house of Mrs. Jane Davis in Albany and he brought with him the piano and furniture for his rooms.
Mrs. Davis, under section 71 of the Lien Law (Laws of 1897, chap. 418), acquired a lien upon the piano for the hoard which she was furnishing from day to day to Mrs. Mann, her husband and son.
I think the evidence clearly shows that Mrs. Davis was a pledgee .in good faith of the piano.

notes: Opinion states the family left Mrs. Davis's boarding house in June 1898 but does not give the date they began boarding there (piano purchased 1895); actual occupancy appears to have run multiple years, which none of nights/weeks/months captures, so left as unclear.

court: Supreme Court, Appellate Division, First Department
holding_summary: Corporate self-dealing accounting action; held that stockholders' ratification of an officer's arrangement to rent his personal automobile to his own corporation estopped the corporation from repudiating the arrangement.
notes: Selector matched on generic 'right to lease'/self-contracting language regarding a corporate officer renting his automobile; no dwelling, lodging, or boarding content.

court: Supreme Court, Appellate Division, Second Department
holding_summary: Enjoined a landowner from maintaining a detached private garage in violation of a covenant restricting the lot to a single dwelling house.
notes: Restrictive-covenant dispute over an accessory garage structure; no compensated occupancy or paying-occupant issue.

court: Supreme Court, Appellate Division, First Department
holding_summary: Enjoined a lot owner from converting a private dwelling into a store-front tailoring establishment with apartments above, as a violation of a partition-sale restrictive covenant limiting the block to private dwellings.
notes: Defendant's planned conversion included 'apartments' on upper floors, but the dispute is about covenant enforcement against a business conversion, not about the legal character of paying lodgers/boarders.

court: Supreme Court, Appellate Division, First Department
holding_summary: Denied injunctive enforcement of a residential-use restrictive covenant as to the rear portion of a lot where enforcement would not benefit the plaintiff but would seriously harm the defendant.
notes: Long restrictive-covenant/title dispute concerning residential-use restrictions and boundary lines; no lodging or boarding-house content.

cite: Beuchamp v. Excelsior Brick Co., 143 A.D. 48
court: Supreme Court, Appellate Division, Second Department
holding_summary: Dismissed a tenant's-wife's nuisance claim against a landlord for injuries from a landslide into an adjoining clay pit that existed openly when the tenancy was entered and renewed.
notes: Landlord-tenant nuisance/tort case about premises safety near a clay-pit excavation; not about compensated lodging or its regulation despite general landlord-tenant discussion.

court: Supreme Court, Appellate Division, First Department
holding_summary: Held that a wife's claim to her share of rents and profits appropriated by her husband as co-tenant by the entirety sounds in an action at law for money had and received, not equity.
notes: Dispute between husband and wife over rents/profits of jointly held real estate; no letting-to-third-parties or lodging issue presented.

cite: People ex rel. Moskowitz v. Jenkins, 140 A.D. 786
court: Supreme Court, Appellate Division, Third Department
holding_summary: Upheld as constitutional a statute requiring a municipal license for transient 'bankrupt stock' sales and sustained a $100 license fee as within the police power.
notes: Police-power licensing case about transient retail 'fire/bankrupt sale' merchants; no lodging-house or boarding-house content despite selector match on general regulation language.
